options.name: GitHub Releases on a NEW PUBLIC repo (e.g. bmisho/studiovd-library). Recommended primary host
options.limits: Up to 1000 assets per release. Each file must be under 2 GiB. The docs say: 'There is no limit on the total size of a release, nor bandwidth usage.' [high, docs plus github/docs data variables release_asset_limit='1000' and max_file_size='2 GiB']. The Acceptable Use Policies section 9 'Excessive Bandwidth Use' still lets GitHub throttle file hosting or suspend accounts whose use is 'significantly excessive' compared with similar users [high]. Immutable releases are available on Free accounts: once published, assets cannot be modified or deleted, the tag is locked, and a release attestation is generated [high]. A stable 'latest' URL exists: /releases/latest/download/<asset> [high]. 'Latest' is chosen automatically from date and version unless a release is created with make_latest=false (gh CLI: --latest=false) [high, gh CLI source]. Anyone who downloads needs read access to the repo. bmisho/StudioVD is PRIVATE (api.github.com returned "private": true on 2026-10-09), so its releases cannot serve anonymous app downloads [high]. Downloads redirect to a short-lived signed URL on a *.githubusercontent.com host. Third parties report an expiry of about 300 s and Range support there. GitHub does not document either [medium/low]. The May 2025 unauthenticated rate limits name cloning, the REST API and raw.githubusercontent.com. Whether release-asset downloads are counted is UNKNOWN. The REST API is limited to 60 requests/h per IP when unauthenticated, so the app must never use the API to discover releases [high].
options.pros: Free. No documented bandwidth cap. Immutable releases and attestations suit a signed catalog. Fits the existing GitHub account and Actions/gh CLI publishing. Per-asset size (2 GiB) is far above any sensible pack size. The stable latest/download URL lets the app find the index without calling the API.
options.cons: Needs a separate public repo, because the main repo is private. Corporate firewalls often block github.com or *.githubusercontent.com (this research sandbox blocks github.com HTML pages). No custom domain. Throttling behaviour is undocumented. The redirect target host has changed over time (objects.githubusercontent.com, release-assets.githubusercontent.com), so allowlists need updating [medium]. Pack releases must be created with --latest=false, or they can take over the 'latest' pointer.

options.name: Separate GitHub repo served via raw.githubusercontent.com
options.limits: Git warns above 50 MiB per file and blocks above 100 MiB. Browser uploads are capped at 25 MiB. Repos should 'ideally' stay under 1 GB, and under 5 GB is 'strongly recommended' [high]. For large files the docs point you to Releases instead. With Git LFS, raw serves only the pointer file. LFS downloads count against the owner's bandwidth, with 10 GiB/month free on Free/Pro [high]. Since May 2025, unauthenticated raw downloads are rate-limited. Exact thresholds are NOT documented: community posts cite 60/h for the API, and an unofficial figure of about 5000/h/IP for raw [medium/low]. Observed on 2026-10-09: Range returns 206 with a strong ETag and Cache-Control max-age=300 (up to 5 minutes stale). One request got HTTP 429 from this sandbox's shared IP [high, observed].
options.pros: Simplest publishing (git push). Per-file URLs. Range and ETag work. Fastly CDN. Good enough for a small index.json or thumbnails mirror if URLs are pinned to a commit SHA.
options.cons: Not meant for binary distribution. The 100 MiB per-file cap and every pack revision stay in git history forever. 429s are observed and thresholds undocumented. The 5-minute cache can serve a new index.json with an old index.json.minisig, so verification fails unless URLs are pinned to a commit SHA. LFS bandwidth is billed.
options.cost: $0. LFS beyond the 10 GiB/month free bandwidth and storage is billed [high].

options.name: GitLab.com (generic package registry, linked from Releases)
options.limits: Generic package max file size on GitLab.com is 5 GB [high]. The package registry is NOT counted in the 10 GiB per-project storage limit, which covers repo plus LFS only [high]. A release asset link points to the package file; the API returns direct_asset_url [high, observed for gitlab-org/cli v1.122.0]. Rate limits in effect today: unauthenticated traffic 500 requests/min per IP, 'GitLab package hosting system requests' 1,000/min per IP, all traffic 2,000/min per IP [high]. PROPOSED and not yet enforced (brownouts announced in advance): tier-aware limits that cut unauthenticated traffic to 60 requests/HOUR per IP [high, docs]. Downloads go through /api/v4/projects/:id/packages/generic/..., so they would likely fall under the anonymous API limit [medium]. Range returned 206 on a real generic package on 2026-10-09 [high, observed]. SHA-256 checksums are computed and stored for uploaded files [high].
options.pros: Free. Large files. Server-side SHA-256. Range works. Independent of GitHub, so useful as a mirror.
options.cons: The proposed 60 req/h per IP for anonymous users would break many users behind one corporate NAT. Downloads use API paths (cache-control: no-cache, observed). Needs a second account and CI.
options.cost: $0 on the Free tier for a public project [high].

options.name: Cloudflare R2 behind a custom domain. Recommended secondary mirror
options.limits: Unlimited storage and objects per bucket. Object size up to 4.995 TiB. Single-part upload up to 4.995 GiB [high]. The managed r2.dev URL 'is not intended for production usage': it has a variable rate limit (hundreds of requests/s, then 429) and bandwidth throttling. Production needs a custom domain, which must be a zone in the same Cloudflare account (full setup or partial CNAME setup) [high]. The Cloudflare cache's max cacheable file size is 512 MB on Free/Pro/Business [high]. The 2023 terms update allows large non-HTML files on the CDN when they are hosted on R2 [medium-high, Cloudflare blog]. Range support was not tested in this research [medium: R2 implements the S3 GetObject API].
options.pros: Zero egress fees. Own domain: stable URLs that are easy to allowlist in corporate networks and not tied to GitHub's throttling. The same object layout works as a drop-in mirror. Analytics, WAF and caching are available.
options.cons: Needs a domain with DNS on Cloudflare, plus upload credentials and tooling (wrangler/rclone/S3 API). Whether a payment method is required for the free tier is UNKNOWN (not verified). Keep packs under 512 MB so the free-plan cache can cache them.
options.cost: Standard storage $0.015/GB-month. Class A ops (writes/lists) $4.50/million. Class B ops (GetObject/HeadObject) $0.36/million. Egress free. Free tier per month: 10 GB-month storage, 1M Class A, 10M Class B. Usage is rounded up to the next billing unit [high]. Worked example (hypothetical usage, documented prices): a 5 GB library with 10,000 full installs/month at about 30 GETs each is 300k Class B ops, so $0 inside the free tier. A domain registration is extra (price not researched).

options.name: Backblaze B2 (optionally fronted by Cloudflare or bunny.net)
options.limits: From search results; the pricing page was NOT fetched directly [medium]. Pay-as-you-go storage about $6.95/TB per 30 days (one Backblaze page shows $6/TB, an inconsistency). First 10 GB free. Free egress up to 3x average monthly storage, then $0.01/GB. Unlimited free egress through partner CDNs (Cloudflare, Fastly, bunny.net and others).
options.pros: Cheap storage. S3-compatible. Partner CDN egress is free.
options.cons: More moving parts than R2 for the same result. Pricing details need checking on the live page.

options.name: jsDelivr (CDN proxy for GitHub/npm). Thumbnails or index mirror only
options.limits: GitHub-sourced packages over 150 MB, or single files over 20 MB, are not supported by default [high, README]. No bandwidth or request limits [high]. The terms prohibit using it as a 'general-purpose file or media hosting service', but say 'apps, or games with a large number of assets' are legitimate [high]. Files are permanently cached once requested [high].
options.pros: Free global CDN. A good fallback for small files (index, thumbnails).
options.cons: Pack zips over 20 MB are not supported from GitHub. Policy grey zone for binary packs. cdn.jsdelivr.net was blocked in this research sandbox, a reminder that corporate filters block CDNs too.

options.name: GitHub Pages (index/thumbnails only)
options.limits: Published site at most 1 GB. Soft bandwidth limit of 100 GB/month. 429 rate limiting possible. Source repo recommended under 1 GB. Not allowed as hosting for commercial SaaS or e-commerce [high].
options.pros: Free. Custom domain possible. Fixed URL for index.json.
options.cons: Too small for packs. The *.github.io domain is often filtered (blocked in this sandbox).

options.name: Hugging Face Hub dataset repo. Not recommended
options.limits: Public storage is free on a 'best-effort' basis. Files should be split into chunks under 200 GB; 500 GB is the hard per-file limit. HF asks that large uploads be 'as useful to the community as possible', meaning the AI community [high].
options.cons: Purpose mismatch (an ML hub). huggingface.co is blocked by some network filters, including this sandbox.
options.cost: $0 for public repos. Paid add-ons cost $12/TB/month [high].

recommended_hosting:
Primary host: GitHub Releases on a NEW PUBLIC repo, e.g. bmisho/studiovd-library [high confidence this is needed: bmisho/StudioVD is private, and release downloads need read access]. Turn on 'immutable releases' for that repo. The repo holds the pack sources, the build scripts and a CI workflow; binaries go only into release assets, never into git history.

Release layout:
(a) One immutable release per pack version, tag 'pack-<packId>-v<semver>'. It contains <packId>-<ver>.zip and its detached <packId>-<ver>.zip.minisig. It is always created with make_latest=false (gh release create --latest=false), so it never takes the 'latest' pointer.
(b) One immutable release per catalog publish, tag 'catalog-<sequence>', marked latest. It contains index.json, index.json.minisig and thumbs-<sequence>.zip.
(c) The app has one baked-in entry point: https://github.com/bmisho/studiovd-library/releases/latest/download/index.json (plus .minisig). This is a documented stable URL that needs no REST API call, so it avoids the 60 req/h unauthenticated API limit.

Secondary mirror (add when needed: if GitHub throttles, or corporate users report github.com blocked): a Cloudflare R2 bucket behind a custom domain (for example library.<your-domain>), using the same relative object layout. Within the free tier it costs about $0 plus the domain, and egress is free.

Third and fourth paths, so corporate and air-gapped users are not stranded:
- A user-configurable mirror base URL, for example an internal Artifactory/Nexus raw repo or any static HTTP server.
- 'Import pack from file…': a pack zip plus its .minisig, downloaded with a browser (browsers handle PAC and NTLM proxies) or copied from a USB drive.

All transports are treated as UNTRUSTED. Trust comes only from the minisign signature on index.json and on each pack, checked against public keys compiled into the app, plus the SHA-256 and size in the signed index. That is why mirrors can be added freely.

Not recommended:
- raw.githubusercontent.com for packs (100 MiB file cap, git history bloat, undocumented 429s, 5-minute cache).
- GitLab generic packages as primary (proposed limit of 60 anonymous requests/hour per IP). It is acceptable as an extra mirror.
- jsDelivr or Pages for packs (20 MB file / 1 GB site limits). Both are fine for index/thumbs only.
- Hugging Face (purpose mismatch).

Keep each pack under about 200 MB. This is a design choice, not a host limit: it keeps resume and re-verification cheap and stays well under Cloudflare's 512 MB free-plan cacheable size. Ship thumbnails as ONE bundle per catalog, so browsing the catalog costs 3 requests rather than hundreds.

Nothing is bundled in the installer, per the user's 'available for download … only'. The built-in schematic primitives, such as the MNA element stamps, remain app code: packs carry parameters and data only, never code (CLAUDE.md forbids eval).

crates.name: reqwest
crates.purpose: HTTP client for all downloads, run from Rust only. Use default-features=false with features ["rustls","http2","system-proxy","stream"]. Do NOT enable gzip/brotli/zstd on this client, so Range offsets refer to raw bytes. 0.13.x is already in Cargo.lock via tauri 2.12.2, so this adds no duplicate reqwest version. MSRV 1.85; the local toolchain is 1.97. Released 2026-09-08 [high, crates.io API].

crates.name: rustls-platform-verifier
crates.purpose: Verifies certificates against the OS trust store. Pulled in transitively by the reqwest 'rustls' feature, which uses it by default since reqwest 0.13.0. On Windows it uses the Windows certificate store and the Windows verification API (with revocation). On Linux it uses the system CA bundle found via openssl-probe, plus webpki [high, README].

crates.name: rustls
crates.purpose: Transitive dependency. Only add it directly if you choose the ring crypto provider (reqwest feature 'rustls-no-provider' plus rustls 'ring', then install the provider at startup) to avoid the aws-lc-sys build. reqwest panics at client build if no provider is installed [high, reqwest v0.13.5 source].

crates.name: tokio
crates.purpose: Async file I/O (fs, io-util), Semaphore for download concurrency, select! for cancellation. Already part of Tauri's runtime: use tauri::async_runtime::spawn.

crates.name: sha2
crates.purpose: Streaming SHA-256 of each downloaded file, and of extracted entries checked against pack.json. 0.11 is a new major version (digest 0.11), released 2026-03-25.

crates.name: hex
crates.purpose: Hex encoding and decoding for SHA-256 strings.

crates.name: minisign-verify
crates.purpose: Verifies the minisign signatures on index.json and on each pack. Zero dependencies. Supports pre-hashed (BLAKE2b) signatures and streaming verification of large files. Exposes the trusted comment after verification. This is the same signature format as the Tauri updater, which itself depends on ^0.2. Released 2026-09-25 [high].

crates.name: ed25519-dalek
crates.purpose: Alternative ONLY, not recommended for v1: raw Ed25519 would need custom signing tooling, and 3.0.0 is a fresh major (2026-07-06). License BSD-3-Clause.

crates.name: zip
crates.purpose: Extracts packs by iterating entries manually: enclosed_name(), is_symlink() rejected, byte-counted size limits. 9.0.0 was published TODAY (2026-10-09); 8.6.0 (2026-04-25) is the previous stable; both MSRV 1.88. Never call extract() with defaults: in 9.0.0 the default SymlinkExtractAction on unix/windows is ExtractRecursiveInFolder. CVE-2025-29787 / RUSTSEC-2025-0168 (symlink path traversal in extract) was fixed in 2.3.0 [high].

crates.name: tempfile
crates.purpose: Unique staging directories inside the library root, so rename stays on the same volume.

crates.name: fs4
crates.purpose: available_space(path) before downloading and extracting [high, source]. Locking does not need this crate: std File::lock/try_lock have been stable since Rust 1.89.0.

crates.name: wiremock (dev)
crates.purpose: Local mock HTTP server for cargo tests: 200/206/416/429+Retry-After, redirects, truncated bodies, wrong hash, cancel mid-stream. mockito 1.7.2 is an alternative.

crates.name: tauri-plugin-http
crates.purpose: NOT recommended. Checked for comparison: depends on reqwest ^0.12.16 (a second reqwest), default TLS feature rustls-tls (webpki roots), MSRV 1.90.

crates.name: tauri-plugin-upload
crates.purpose: NOT recommended. Checked for comparison: reqwest ^0.12, default rustls-tls (webpki roots), MSRV 1.90 (alpha: 1.95).

download_implementation.rust_vs_plugin:
Verdict: write our own Rust module, src-tauri/src/library/* (download.rs, verify.rs, extract.rs, index.rs, state.rs, each under 200 lines), with thin #[tauri::command] wrappers in src-tauri/src/commands/library.rs and typed TS wrappers in src/lib/tauri/library.ts (mockable for Playwright) [high]. Reasons:

(1) DEPENDENCIES. Cargo.lock already contains reqwest 0.13.5, pulled in by tauri 2.12.2 with no TLS features, so using reqwest 0.13 ourselves just turns on TLS features on that crate. tauri-plugin-http 2.8.1 requires reqwest ^0.12.16 and tauri-plugin-upload 2.5.0 requires reqwest ^0.12, which would compile a second reqwest/hyper-rustls stack [high: lockfile plus crates.io dependency API].

(2) TRUST STORE. reqwest 0.13.0 made rustls the default TLS backend, with the aws-lc-rs provider and rustls-platform-verifier (the OS trust store) [high, CHANGELOG]. Both plugins default to the reqwest 0.12 feature rustls-tls, which maps to rustls-tls-webpki-roots: a bundled Mozilla root list that ignores a corporate CA installed in the OS store. Avoiding that means switching plugin features to native-tls or rustls-tls-native-roots [high: crates.io feature maps].

(3) tauri-plugin-upload's download(), read from the upload-v2.5.0 source:
- creates a new reqwest::Client on every call
- uses File::create, which truncates the file, so there is no resume
- has no cancellation and no checksum
- takes BOTH the URL and the destination path from the webview, and the plugin source has no scope check, so the webview can choose where on disk to write
- reports progress over ipc::Channel, which is the only part worth copying [high]
A 3.0.0 alpha line exists, so expect API churn.

(4) tauri-plugin-http is a JS fetch() proxy with URL allowlist scopes. Redirect hops are only checked if 'scopeRedirects' is enabled [high, plugins-workspace v2 source]. The response body returns to JS, so a pack zip would cross IPC, which breaks CLAUDE.md §6 ('Large binaries never cross IPC'). The webview would also be originating network requests, against the offline-first design.

(5) Our own command takes IDs, not URLs. Rust resolves URLs from the verified index plus compiled-in and user-set mirrors, so a compromised webview cannot make the app fetch arbitrary URLs or write arbitrary paths. It also gives us Range resume, If-Range, streaming SHA-256, cancellation, a semaphore, retries honoring Retry-After, a disk-space check, and atomic install in one place, unit-testable headlessly per CLAUDE.md §8.

Build notes:
- reqwest 'rustls' uses aws-lc-rs. On x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, aws-lc-sys needs a C compiler (MSVC, which Tauri needs anyway) plus NASM, OR the env var AWS_LC_SYS_PREBUILT_NASM=1 (prebuilt objects are used only when NASM is absent). On Linux only a C compiler is needed, with no CMake [high, aws-lc-rs book].
- If that is a nuisance in CI, use features ["rustls-no-provider",...] plus rustls with 'ring', and call rustls::crypto::ring::default_provider().install_default() before building the Client.

Effort estimate (mine, not measured): 400-600 lines of Rust plus tests.
download_implementation.integrity_and_signing:
Chain of trust, with a confidence level on each design element:

1) KEYS. Generate two minisign Ed25519 keypairs (minisign -G, or rsign2): K1 primary and K2 backup. Embed BOTH public keys as a Rust const in src-tauri/src/library/keys.rs. Do not put them in tauri.conf.json or the frontend, since only Rust verifies. A minisign signature carries an 8-byte key ID, so the verifier picks the matching trusted key. Keep these keys SEPARATE from the Tauri updater key (Phase 13 'optional updater'), so one compromise does not cover both code and data. Store the K1 secret key password-protected and offline, on the maintainer's machine or a hardware-backed vault. Sign index.json locally: it is small, and signing locally keeps the key out of CI. CI may build packs and print their SHA-256. K2 stays offline and unused until rotation.
As the Tauri updater docs warn for their key, losing the private key means you cannot publish anything existing installs will accept, so keep a backup [high, v2.tauri.app/plugin/updater].

2) SIGNED INDEX. Download index.json and index.json.minisig, with a hard size cap (for example 16 MiB) applied BEFORE parsing. Verify with minisign_verify::PublicKey::verify(bytes, &sig, false). allow_legacy=false accepts only pre-hashed signatures, which minisign creates by default.
Only AFTER verification, read the trusted comment, for example 'studiovd-index\tsequence:42\tschema:1\ttimestamp:…'. Check that its sequence and schema equal the JSON's sequence and schemaVersion. This copies the Tauri updater's verify_signed_version pattern: the trusted comment is used only after the global signature checks out, which stops mix-and-match of a new version label with old content [high, updater.rs source].
Parse JSON only after verification, then validate it with serde (strict, deny_unknown_fields optional) and, on the TS side, with zod.

3) ROLLBACK and FREEZE PROTECTION. Persist the highest verified sequence in library/state.json and reject any index with a lower sequence. Offer an explicit 'Reset catalog trust state' in Settings for recovery. An optional expiresAt is ADVISORY only: show 'catalog is N days old', never block, because the app is offline-first.

4) PER-FILE INTEGRITY. The signed index gives sha256 and size for every pack zip and the thumbs bundle. The downloader hashes while streaming and rejects on any size or hash mismatch before extraction. For defense in depth and offline import, each pack also has a detached <zip>.minisig, so 'Import pack from file' verifies without the index, and any mirror is untrusted. Inside each pack, pack.json lists sha256 for every entry. These are checked during extraction. GLBs are named <sha256>.glb, which matches the content addressing in PLAN.md §1.1.3, so inserting into a project is a plain copy.

5) KEY ROTATION. App vN ships {K1, K2}, and K1 keeps signing. Once most users are on version N or later, switch signing to K2 and ship vN+1 with {K2, K3-new-backup}. For a smooth overlap you may publish two signature files (index.json.minisig from K1 and index.json.k2.minisig from K2), and the client accepts either.
If a key is COMPROMISED: release an app update removing that key immediately. Installs that are not updated stay exposed until they update. This is inherent to offline-first with no online revocation. The blast radius is limited because packs are data, not code. That is why parsers must be hardened: zip limits, schema validation, no symlinks, a file-type allowlist (.glb .json .webp .png .md/.txt), and caps on GLB size and triangle count.

6) WHY minisign over raw ed25519-dalek or TUF. Minisign brings CLIs, trusted comments, streaming pre-hashed verification, a zero-dependency verifier, and the same format as Tauri's updater. Raw Ed25519 would need custom tooling. TUF (crate 'tough' 0.24.0) adds role delegation and timestamp/snapshot metadata, which is overkill for v1 but a valid upgrade path.

7) HOST-SIDE. GitHub immutable releases stop assets being swapped after publication, and a release attestation is generated [high]. This is complementary, not a substitute: the app must not trust it.
download_implementation.resumable_and_progress:
Design, all in Rust (download.rs):

- STAGING. Write to <library>/staging/<sha256>.part, with a sidecar <sha256>.part.json holding {url, etag, lastModified, expectedSize}. Staging is inside the library root so the final rename stays on the same volume. On Linux, ~/.cache can be another filesystem or tmpfs.

- RESUME. If a .part exists, re-hash its existing bytes into a fresh Sha256 (sha2 hasher state cannot be persisted in a portable way), then send GET with 'Range: bytes=<len>-' and 'If-Range: <etag>' (or Last-Modified).
  - 206 with a Content-Range start equal to len: append.
  - 200: the server ignored or invalidated the range, so truncate and restart.
  - 416: verify the existing file. If the hash is OK, done; otherwise delete it and restart.
  - Never reuse a stored signed redirect URL. Always re-request the stable URL and let reqwest follow redirects again (default Policy::limited(10)). reqwest strips only Authorization/Cookie/Proxy-Authorization/WWW-Authenticate on cross-host redirects, so the Range header survives [high, redirect.rs].
  - GitHub's signed redirect URLs reportedly expire after about 300 s [low/medium, third-party captures]. Range support on them is not documented, so treat a 200 response as normal.
  - Verified on 2026-10-09: raw.githubusercontent.com and GitLab generic package downloads return 206 for Range requests [high, observed].

- FINALIZE. Compare the size and SHA-256 with the signed index. On match, fsync, then rename to staging/<sha256>.zip and extract (see the storage field). On mismatch, delete the .part and retry once from zero, then surface an error that names the host.

- PROGRESS. Use tauri::ipc::Channel<LibraryEvent> passed as a command argument. Tauri's docs say channels 'are designed to be fast and deliver ordered data' and are used internally 'for streaming operations such as download progress', whereas events evaluate JS and are JSON-only [high, v2.tauri.app/develop/calling-frontend/#channels]. Events: Started{jobId,total}, Progress{jobId,bytes,total,bytesPerSec}, Verifying, Extracting{done,total}, Done, Failed{code,message,retryable}, Cancelled.
  Throttle Progress to at most one event every 100 ms or 1 MiB, so the store does not re-render the UI per chunk. Progress lives in SESSION state (CLAUDE.md §4), keyed by jobId.

- CANCELLATION. Keep a CancellationToken per job in a Mutex<HashMap<JobId, Token>> in Tauri managed state. library_cancel(jobId) triggers it, and the stream loop runs tokio::select! { _ = token.cancelled() => …, chunk = stream.next() => … }. Cancel keeps the .part for later resume unless the user picks 'Discard'. App shutdown cancels all jobs.

- CONCURRENCY. One global tokio::sync::Semaphore with 2 permits for pack downloads (index and thumbs are fetched serially first). There are no multi-connection segmented downloads: that is polite to hosts with rate limits and simpler. A queue UI shows waiting jobs.

- RETRIES and TIMEOUTS. connect_timeout 15 s and read_timeout 30 s, with no total timeout (big files on slow links). These ClientBuilder methods exist in reqwest 0.13.5 [high]; the values are suggestions. Exponential backoff with jitter, at most 5 attempts, honoring Retry-After on 429/503 (GitLab documents Retry-After on 429). Errors are classified retryable or fatal: TLS UnknownIssuer and proxy 407 are fatal, with guidance.

- DISK SPACE. Check fs4::available_space(library_root) >= zipSize + extractedSize (from the index) + 10% before starting.

- USER-AGENT. 'StudioVD/<version> (+https://github.com/bmisho/studiovd-library)'. Never include user identifiers.

- SINGLE WRITER. Take a std::fs::File::try_lock on <library>/LOCK (stable since Rust 1.89.0), so two app instances do not install at once. PLAN.md 5.4 already plans single-instance forwarding, but keep the lock anyway.
download_implementation.proxy_and_certificates_windows_linux:
PROXY, reqwest 0.13 with feature 'system-proxy', which uses hyper-util's Matcher::from_system [high, hyper-util v0.1.21 source]:

- Both OSes: env vars ALL_PROXY/all_proxy, HTTPS_PROXY/https_proxy, HTTP_PROXY/http_proxy and NO_PROXY/no_proxy are read first, curl-style.

- WINDOWS: if the env vars are unset, it reads HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Internet Settings, using ProxyEnable, ProxyServer (formats http=…;https=…;socks=… or a single host:port) and ProxyOverride for the bypass list. It does NOT evaluate PAC scripts (AutoConfigURL) or WPAD auto-detect; no such code exists in the matcher [high, source read].

- LINUX: env vars ONLY. GNOME/KDE proxy settings (gsettings/kioslaverc) are not read [high: from_system only adds macOS and Windows]. Desktop-launched apps often do not inherit shell env vars.

- PROXY AUTH: reqwest offers Proxy::basic_auth and Proxy::custom_http_auth (a static header) only. There is no NTLM/Negotiate/Kerberos, a common corporate setup [high: no such code in proxy.rs].

- MITIGATIONS, in Settings > Network:
  (a) Mode: System (default) / Manual URL / No proxy. Manual uses reqwest::Proxy::all(url) with optional basic credentials, kept in memory or in the OS keychain.
  (b) A 'Test connection' button that fetches index.json.minisig and shows a precise diagnosis (DNS, TCP, 407, TLS unknown issuer, 403/429).
  (c) A custom mirror URL (internal Artifactory/Nexus/static server).
  (d) 'Import pack from file' with a detached .minisig: download in the browser, which handles PAC and NTLM.
  (e) Future option on Windows: resolve PAC via WinHTTP (WinHttpGetIEProxyConfigForCurrentUser / WinHttpGetProxyForUrl, documented Win32 APIs) [medium; not prototyped].

CERTIFICATES:

- RECOMMENDED: rustls with rustls-platform-verifier, the reqwest 0.13 default.
  - WINDOWS: verifies with the Windows certificate store and the Windows verification API, including revocation, so enterprise root CAs pushed by Group Policy for TLS-inspecting proxies are trusted automatically [high, README table].
  - LINUX: loads the system CA bundle found by openssl-probe (via rustls-native-certs) and verifies with webpki, without revocation. SSL_CERT_FILE is honored first. The trust store is read once at startup. A corporate CA must be installed into the distro store (for example update-ca-certificates or update-ca-trust) and the app restarted [high, rustls-platform-verifier and rustls-native-certs READMEs].
  - ESCAPE HATCH: Settings > 'Additional trusted CA certificate (PEM)', applied with ClientBuilder::tls_certs_merge(certs). It merges with the platform roots and never replaces them. Never offer 'disable verification'.

- native-tls alternative: SChannel on Windows (also uses the OS store) and OpenSSL on Linux. That adds a runtime libssl dependency and so-version issues for AppImage. No advantage over the platform verifier for this app [medium].

- AVOID webpki-roots (the default of both Tauri plugins): it ignores corporate roots, and root updates need app releases [high, rustls-platform-verifier README comparison table].
download_implementation.storage_paths_windows_linux:
Use appLocalDataDir as the root, with a 'library' subfolder. Tauri 2.12.2 resolves it as local_data_dir()/<identifier> [high, crates/tauri/src/path/desktop.rs]:

WINDOWS (FOLDERID_LocalAppData):
- appLocalDataDir: C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\com.studiovd.desktop
- Library root: C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\com.studiovd.desktop\library
- For reference, appDataDir is FOLDERID_RoamingAppData: C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming\com.studiovd.desktop. Do NOT put the library there: Roaming data follows roaming profiles and corporate quotas [medium: Windows general knowledge].
- NOTE: appCacheDir on Windows is ALSO FOLDERID_LocalAppData/<identifier>, the SAME folder as appLocalDataDir [high, desktop.rs docs].
- Tauri's source states that appLocalDataDir is also the default webview data directory on Windows and Linux (the WebView2 EBWebView folder) [high].
- So keep strictly separate subfolders: library/, workspaces/ (PLAN.md's app-cache workspaces), and the webview data. Never 'clear cache' by deleting the root.

LINUX:
- appLocalDataDir = appDataDir = $XDG_DATA_HOME/com.studiovd.desktop, default ~/.local/share/com.studiovd.desktop. Library root: ~/.local/share/com.studiovd.desktop/library
- appCacheDir = $XDG_CACHE_HOME/com.studiovd.desktop, default ~/.cache/com.studiovd.desktop [high].
- .deb and AppImage use these XDG paths. A Flatpak build would remap XDG_DATA_HOME into ~/.var/app/<app-id>/ [medium; not a current target].

LAYOUT under library/:
- LOCK: std File::try_lock
- state.json: highest sequence, installed packs, mirror settings. Written atomically: write temp, fsync, rename.
- catalog/index.json and catalog/index.json.minisig: the last VERIFIED index, re-verified on load.
- catalog/thumbs/<sequence>/<packId>/<componentId>.webp
- staging/: .part files, verified zips, extraction temp dirs
- packs/<packId>/<version>/: pack.json, components/<componentId>/component.json, geometry/<sha256>.glb, LICENSE, ATTRIBUTION.md
- trash/: deferred deletes

INSTALL is atomic:
1. Extract into staging/x-<random> (tempfile).
2. Validate every entry: enclosed_name() must be Some, reject symlinks and absolute or '..' paths, enforce an allowlist of extensions and names.
3. Reject Windows-reserved names (CON, NUL, AUX, COM1…) and trailing dots or spaces, plus names that collide case-insensitively.
4. Enforce limits: entry count, per-entry and total uncompressed bytes counted while copying, not trusted from headers, and a compression-ratio cap.
5. Check every entry's SHA-256 against pack.json, then fsync.
6. Rename to packs/<id>/<ver>, then update state.json.
On Windows, antivirus or the indexer may briefly hold handles. Retry the rename and delete with backoff, and move undeletable folders to trash/ for cleanup on next start [medium]. Startup sweeps staging/x-* and trash/.

PATH LENGTH: keep pack IDs to [a-z0-9-]{1,32} and versions short. A typical full path, C:\Users\<20 chars>\AppData\Local\com.studiovd.desktop\library\packs\<32>\<16>\geometry\<64-hex>.glb, is about 190 characters, under the legacy 260 MAX_PATH [high arithmetic; the MAX_PATH rule is Windows general knowledge].

RELOCATION and PORTABLE MODE:
- Tauri 2.12 adds config app.appDirectoriesOverride, which redirects all app_*_dir APIs, for example for a portable install next to the exe [high, schema].
- A user-chosen 'Library location' setting (for a bigger drive) is also feasible. The asset-protocol scope must then be widened at runtime with the asset protocol scope API [medium: API not re-verified here].

FREE SPACE: check with fs4::available_space before installing. Show per-pack disk usage, and offer Remove and 'Remove old versions'.
download_implementation.tauri_capabilities_and_csp:
Principle: the webview makes ZERO network requests. All HTTP happens in Rust, and the webview only sees IDs, progress events and local asset URLs.

1) NO network plugins. Do not add tauri-plugin-http or tauri-plugin-upload. Library work needs no fs-plugin permissions, because Rust reads and writes. The existing 'opener:default' permission only hands URLs to the system browser (for example license links), which is not a webview request.

2) CUSTOM COMMANDS: library_get_state, library_refresh_index, library_install(packId, version, onEvent: Channel), library_cancel(jobId), library_remove(packId, version), library_import_file(), library_get_component(componentRef), library_insert_into_project(componentRef).
- They take IDs, never URLs or arbitrary paths.
- library_import_file opens the file dialog FROM RUST (the tauri-plugin-dialog Rust API), so the path never comes from JS.
- By default, all registered app commands are allowed in all windows [high, v2.tauri.app/security/capabilities]. Restrict them with tauri_build::Attributes::new().app_manifest(AppManifest::new().commands(&[…])) in build.rs, and grant 'allow-library-*' only to window 'main' in capabilities/default.json [high].
- Progress channels (tauri::ipc::Channel) need no extra permission.

3) ASSET PROTOCOL, so the viewport loads library GLBs and thumbnails without IPC:
- Enable the Cargo feature tauri/protocol-asset. In 2.12.2 it implies 'http-range', so the protocol serves Range requests [high, tauri Cargo.toml].
- Set app.security.assetProtocol = { enable: true, scope: ['$APPLOCALDATA/library/packs/**', '$APPLOCALDATA/library/catalog/thumbs/**', <workspace dir>/** ] } (config schema: AssetProtocolConfig {enable, scope}) [high].
- Do NOT scope '$APPLOCALDATA/**'. That would expose the WebView2/WebKitGTK profile data that lives in the same folder [high, Tauri source comment].
- convertFileSrc() gives 'asset://localhost/…' on Linux and 'http://asset.localhost/…' on Windows, so the CSP lists both forms [high, Tauri docs example].

4) CSP target for Phase 13, replacing csp:null:
default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; worker-src 'self' blob:; connect-src ipc: http://ipc.localhost asset: http://asset.localhost; img-src 'self' asset: http://asset.localhost blob: data:; media-src 'self' asset: http://asset.localhost; font-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'none'; frame-src 'none'
Notes:
- 'wasm-unsafe-eval' is required for WASM (Rapier, occt-import-js) [high, Tauri CSP doc tip].
- three.js GLTFLoader uses fetch, so connect-src must include the asset origins.
- There are NO http(s) origins anywhere, so even an XSS cannot reach the network or exfiltrate.
- Tauri injects nonces and hashes for bundled scripts and styles at compile time [high]. Whether 'unsafe-inline' for styles is really needed depends on the UI libraries; verify in Phase 13 [medium].
- devCsp additionally allows http://localhost:1420 and ws://localhost:1420 for Vite HMR.
- dangerousDisableAssetCspModification stays false.

5) E2E: because every call goes through src/lib/tauri/library.ts, Playwright mocks the commands and simulates Channel events with no network at all, consistent with CLAUDE.md §8.

catalog_index_design:
Three file kinds per catalog publish: index.json plus index.json.minisig, one thumbs-<sequence>.zip, and N pack zips (each with a detached .minisig). Browsing the online catalog costs 3 requests. Installing a pack costs 1 or 2 more.

index.json (signed as exact bytes; the trusted comment repeats sequence and schema):
{"format":"studiovd-library-index","schemaVersion":1,"sequence":42,"generatedAt":"2026-10-09T12:00:00Z","expiresAt":"2027-04-09T00:00:00Z","minAppVersion":"0.4.0","mirrors":["https://github.com/bmisho/studiovd-library/releases/download/","https://library.example.org/"],"thumbs":{"path":"catalog-42/thumbs-42.zip","size":4194304,"sha256":"<64hex>"},"packs":[{"id":"electronics-basic","version":"1.2.0","packFormat":1,"minAppVersion":"0.4.0","title":"Basic electronics","description":"LEDs, resistors, switches, batteries","license":"CC-BY-SA-4.0","attribution":"…","path":"pack-electronics-basic-v1.2.0/electronics-basic-1.2.0.zip","size":73400320,"sha256":"<64hex>","unpackedSize":152043520,"components":[{"id":"led-5mm-red","name":"LED 5 mm red","category":"electronic/optoelectronic/led","tags":["led","tht","5mm"],"domains":["electrical","light"],"thumb":"electronics-basic/led-5mm-red.webp","blockType":"led@1"}]}]}

The numbers above are placeholders, not measurements.

Rules:
1. 'path' is relative. The client tries its mirror list in order: compiled-in mirrors first, then the user mirror, with the index 'mirrors' list only as hints, because the index is trusted only after verification. GitHub release asset URLs flatten naturally to <base>/<tag>/<file>, so the same relative path works on R2 or an internal server.
2. Component summaries live in the index, so search and filter in the Library tab work offline and before any pack is downloaded, using the cached verified index plus thumbnails.
3. Size caps are enforced: index at most 16 MiB, thumbs at most 64 MiB, packs at most the declared size, and the declared size at most 512 MiB (keeping the CDN cacheable).
4. Unknown fields are ignored for forward compatibility. An unknown schemaVersion major makes the client keep the old index and report 'app update required for new catalog'.

Pack zip layout:
- pack.json: {id, version, packFormat, files:[{path, sha256, size}], components:[…]}
- components/<componentId>/component.json:
  - geometry: {asset: '<sha256>.glb', units: 'mm', upAxis: 'Y'}
  - mass: {materialId, density_kg_m3}, or explicit mass and inertia
  - anchors: [{id: 'shaft', frame: {position_mm, quaternion}, kind: 'axis'}, {id: 'mount-1', …}]
  - schematic: {blockType: 'dc-motor@1', ports: [{id, domain: 'electrical' | 'mechanical-rot' | 'fluid' | 'light' | 'data', …}], params: {name: {value, unit}}} with SI units per CLAUDE.md §5
  - bindings: for example LED glow mapped to a light-port output
- geometry/<sha256>.glb: pre-normalized to mm and Y-up, no Draco/meshopt unless the bundled decoders are used.
- thumbs/<componentId>.webp
- LICENSE, ATTRIBUTION.md

Packs contain DATA ONLY: no scripts, no expressions beyond the sandboxed parser's grammar. A pack whose blockType is not built into the running app is shown as 'requires StudioVD ≥ minAppVersion'.

Client-side state: library/state.json holds {highestSequence, installed: {packId: [versions]}, pinned, mirrors, proxy settings reference}. The cached catalog/index.json is re-verified at load: it is cheap and detects on-disk corruption.

Insert into project: copy geometry/<sha256>.glb into the project workspace's geometry/ folder. The name already matches PLAN.md's content-addressed layout, so identical components dedupe automatically. Snapshot component.json into scene.json as a part plus anchors plus a schematic node, with provenance {packId, componentId, version, sha256}. The .stvd bundle is then self-contained and opens on machines without the library.
versioning_and_updates:
IDENTITY and VERSIONS:
- Each pack has a semver version and is IMMUTABLE once published. The host enforces this through GitHub immutable releases. The client enforces it too: if a later index shows the same packId@version with a different sha256, the client rejects that entry and warns.
- MAJOR bump: component IDs, anchor IDs or port IDs removed or renamed, since these break references. MINOR: components added. PATCH: geometry or metadata fixes that keep IDs.
- Component references take the form <packId>/<componentId>@<version>. Schematic behaviour is referenced as blockType@major. Block implementations are app code, so a pack declares minAppVersion and packFormat.
- index.json carries an integer schemaVersion and a monotonically increasing integer sequence. Both are bound into the signed trusted comment.
- Version comparisons use the semver crate 1.0.28.

INSTALL MODEL:
- Packs are installed side by side as packs/<id>/<version>. Keep the newest version plus any version the user pins. 'Remove old versions' is an explicit action.
- Projects never depend on an installed pack: assets are copied in at insert time. So removing or updating packs never breaks a .stvd file.
- 'Update component in project' is explicit and undoable (one zundo entry). It maps anchors and ports by ID and flags mates or wires whose anchors or ports disappeared.

UPDATE CHECKS: no network traffic unless the user asks for it.
- Default: NEVER at startup.
- Triggers:
  (a) the user opens Library > 'Online catalog' or clicks 'Check for updates';
  (b) opt-in setting 'Check for library updates on startup, at most once every 7 days', default OFF;
  (c) installing a pack.
- The first network use shows a one-time consent dialog naming the hosts (github.com and its *.githubusercontent.com download host, plus any mirror).
- A global 'Offline mode: never connect' switch disables everything.
- A check costs 2 small requests (index.json and its .minisig). The thumbs bundle downloads only if its sha256 changed. Use If-None-Match where the host gives ETags (observed on raw.githubusercontent.com). ETag behaviour of GitHub's latest/download redirect is UNKNOWN.
- When newer versions of installed packs exist, show a badge. Updating is always a user click. There is no silent auto-update of data.

OFFLINE BEHAVIOUR:
- The Library tab lists installed packs from state.json, plus the last verified index for browsing, with uninstalled items greyed out and showing their download size.
- With no cached index (first run, nothing bundled): show 'Download component catalog' and 'Import pack from file…'.
- Interrupted downloads resume later from the .part files.
- Network errors show a precise cause plus Retry, and never block design work.

ROLLBACK and STALENESS:
- An index with a sequence lower than the stored highest is rejected.
- expiresAt is advisory only ('catalog is N days old').

PUBLISHING PIPELINE (library repo CI):
1. Build packs: normalize GLBs and validate component.json against the same zod/serde schemas.
2. Validate file names (Windows-reserved names, case collisions, length) and licenses.
3. Compute sha256 values, create the pack releases with --latest=false, and upload the zips.
4. The maintainer signs the zips and index.json locally with minisign, trusted comment 'studiovd-index\tsequence:N\tschema:1'.
5. Create release catalog-N as latest with index.json, its .minisig and thumbs-N.zip.
6. Optionally sync the same tree to R2.
7. A post-publish smoke test downloads latest/download/index.json and verifies it with the public key.

App and library updates are fully decoupled. Library publishing never requires an app release unless it needs a new blockType, packFormat or schemaVersion.
risks: Main repo bmisho/StudioVD is PRIVATE (api.github.com reports "private": true), so its Releases cannot serve anonymous downloads. A separate public library repo, or R2, is required [high].

Corporate networks: github.com and *.githubusercontent.com or CDNs may be blocked (this sandbox blocks github.com pages, cdn.jsdelivr.net and *.github.io). PAC-only proxy setups are not honored: reqwest/hyper-util reads only env vars plus the Windows manual registry proxy, and env vars only on Linux. NTLM/Kerberos proxy auth is unsupported (Basic or a static header only). TLS inspection on Linux needs the corporate CA in the system bundle and an app restart. Mitigations: proxy and extra-CA settings, a custom mirror URL, offline import of signed packs, and a precise connection test [high for the behaviours, from source].

Undocumented or changing rate limits: GitHub's unauthenticated limits since May 2025 (an HTTP 429 from raw.githubusercontent.com was observed during this research). GitLab's PROPOSED 60 requests/hour per IP for anonymous users would break shared-NAT offices. Mitigate by keeping requests minimal (index + sig + one thumbs bundle + one zip per pack), backing off with Retry-After, and keeping a second mirror.

Signing key loss means no catalog or pack update that existing installs will accept. Key compromise means malicious catalogs are accepted until an app update removes the key, with no online revocation in an offline-first app. Mitigations: offline primary key, embedded backup key, separate from the Tauri updater key, a rotation procedure, and parsers hardened so that signed-but-malicious data still cannot escape (no code in packs).

Malicious or malformed archive content: zip-slip via symlinks (history: CVE-2025-29787 / RUSTSEC-2025-0168 in zip extract; zip 9.0.0's default SymlinkExtractAction still extracts in-folder symlinks), decompression bombs, huge or degenerate GLBs, and schema-violating JSON. Mitigations: manual entry iteration, no symlinks, byte-counted limits, an extension allowlist, per-file SHA-256, serde/zod validation, and caps on triangle count and file size before loading in the viewport.

Licensing of redistributed third-party models: attribution and share-alike terms, and vendor CAD terms that forbid redistribution. Needs per-pack SPDX license and attribution in the index and the UI, plus a CI license gate. Content licensing is outside this hosting research [medium].

'latest' pointer hijack: GitHub sets 'latest' automatically by date and version, so a pack release published after a catalog release could become latest and break releases/latest/download/index.json. Always create pack releases with make_latest=false (gh --latest=false). Add a post-publish CI smoke test, and an R2 fixed URL as fallback [high for the GitHub behaviour].

Cache or consistency windows: raw.githubusercontent.com serves max-age=300, and CDNs may cache the 'latest' redirect. That can pair a new index.json with an old .minisig and fail verification. Fetch both files from the same immutable release URL (resolve 'latest' once, then use the tagged URL), and retry once on verify failure.

Resume on GitHub is not documented: the signed redirect URLs reportedly expire after about 300 s, and Range support there is unverified. Always re-request the stable URL, use If-Range, and treat a 200 response as a restart [medium/low].

Windows file-system hazards: antivirus or indexer handles cause rename or delete failures. Also the legacy 260-character MAX_PATH, case-insensitive name collisions, and reserved device names (CON, NUL, …). Mitigations: retries, a trash/ folder, short IDs, and CI name validation [medium].

Wrong storage location: appDataDir on Windows is Roaming (profile sync, quotas), and on Windows appCacheDir equals appLocalDataDir, the same folder that holds the WebView2 profile. A careless 'clear cache' or a broad asset scope could delete or expose webview data. Use explicit subfolders and narrow asset-protocol scopes [high for the path facts].
Partial installs after a crash or power loss: mitigated by staging, fsync, atomic rename, an atomically written state.json, and a startup sweep of staging and trash.

Crate churn: zip 9.0.0 was published on 2026-10-09 (today), sha2 0.11 and ed25519-dalek 3.0 are fresh majors, and Tauri plugins already have 3.0 alphas. Pin exact versions, run cargo-deny/cargo-audit in CI, and prefer zip 8.6.0 until 9.x soaks. Owning the download code limits exposure to plugin API changes.

Windows build friction: reqwest's default rustls provider is aws-lc-rs, which needs NASM on x86_64-pc-windows-msvc unless AWS_LC_SYS_PREBUILT_NASM=1 is set. Alternatively switch to the ring provider via 'rustls-no-provider' [high].

Privacy and offline-first expectations: every download exposes the user's IP and User-Agent to GitHub or Cloudflare, and GitHub publishes per-asset download counts. Users may also expect components on first run, but the library is download-only. Mitigations: consent dialog, offline-mode switch, no identifiers in requests, and a clear empty-state UX. Built-in schematic primitives must work without any pack.

Disk usage growth from a 'whole library' plus side-by-side versions. Show per-pack sizes, keep installs per pack (no all-or-nothing), make 'Remove old versions' explicit, check free space before download, and support library relocation or portable mode (Tauri 2.12 appDirectoriesOverride).

Hosting policy risk: GitHub's AUP section 9 'excessive bandwidth' clause and the jsDelivr or Hugging Face purpose clauses could lead to throttling if the library becomes popular. Keeping an R2 mirror ready (egress free, about $0 at this scale) makes moving hosts a config change rather than an app release.
